answers.core: Same as above: for UI integration we need it to be native, else a plugin is fine.
answers.workaround:
For the command/button itself and handling each track one by one: no, it's a core window

If we tolerate a plugin to run a command that will generate all RESET tracks for all tracks at once (in the current animation or even all animations): yes, it's feasible.

In that, in https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/6417 we mentioned a 3rd party plugin, https://github.com/timothyqiu/godot-animation-resetter, that does exactly the opposite: fill normal tracks with RESET track values. So the other way round should be possible.
